QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_33

question.text: An NPO must be registered under which Section of the Income Tax Act 1961 to even qualify for tax-exempt status, and under which Section can it extend tax deduction to its donors?

answer.text: Section 80C for the NPO; Section 80G for the donor.
Section 12A (or 12AB post-2020) for the NPO's tax-exempt status; Section 80G for the donor's deduction on donation.
Section 10 for the NPO; Section 24 for the donor.
Section 139 for the NPO; Section 56 for the donor.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.2.2(A), 'All NPOs must be registered under Section 12A of the Income Tax Act 1961 and file income tax returns as per the provisions of Income Tax Act, 1961. Upon assessment of these returns, an entity is granted an exemption of tax status for a particular year. An NPO can extend tax deduction to its donors upon approval under Section 80G of the Income Tax Act, 1961.' Post-Finance-Act 2020, 12A registrations were migrated to 12AB with a 5-year validity. The Trap: Option A confuses 80C (individual savings deduction) with the NPO side. Option C invents wrong Sections. Option D confuses filing Section 139 with registration status. Cross-Exam Context: V-A (MF Distributor) treats 80G donor-side deduction. X-A/X-B (IA) advises HNI donors on 80G. XXIV/IFSCA-01 (AML) references FCRA — adjacent to 12AB compliance. Assessor's Pro-Tip: On your initial NPO fieldwork, obtain both the 12AB certificate and the 80G certificate; verify both validity dates fall within or around the ZCZP fund-raising period — expiry of 80G during a public issue invalidates donor deductions and materially affects future fundraising capacity.
